section.content: The machine learning method includes processing a first global image and a first local image through a first expansion pipeline to generate a first expanded global image and a first expanded local image, processing the first global image through a second expansion pipeline to generate a second expanded global image, processing the first expanded global image through a first encoder to generate a first global characterization vector, processing the second expanded global image and the first expanded local image through a second encoder to generate a second global characterization vector and a first local characterization vector, comparing the first global characterization vector and the second global characterization vector to generate a global loss function, comparing the first global characterization vector and the first local characterization vector to generate a hybrid loss function, and adjusting the second encoder according to the global loss function and the hybrid loss function. Thus, the training result is better.

机器学习方法包括：通过第一扩充管道对第一全域影像及第一局部影像进行处理以产生第一扩充全域影像及第一扩充局部影像；通过第二扩充管道对第一全域影像进行处理以产生第二扩充全域影像；通过第一编码器对第一扩充全域影像进行处理以产生第一全域表征向量；通过第二编码器对第二扩充全域影像及第一扩充局部影像进行处理以产生第二全域表征向量及第一局部表征向量；比较第一及第二全域表征向量以产生全域损失函数；比较第一全域表征向量及第一局部表征向量以产生混和损失函数；以及依据全域损失函数及混和损失函数调整第二编码器。如此一来，训练结果较佳。

Machine learning methodTechnical Field

The present disclosure relates to machine learning, and more particularly to a machine learning method.

Background

Self-supervised learning includes a pre-training phase and a fine tuning phase. In the pre-training phase, the user pre-trains the encoder with the unlabeled dataset. However, the pre-training results are poor due to the small differences between the pre-trained images. Therefore, how to overcome the above-mentioned drawbacks is an important subject in the art.

Disclosure of Invention

Embodiments of the present disclosure include a machine learning method. The machine learning method comprises the steps of cutting an original image to generate a first global image, cutting the original image to generate a first local image, processing the first global image through a first expansion pipeline to generate a first expansion global image, processing the first global image through a second expansion pipeline to generate a second expansion global image, processing the first local image through the first expansion pipeline to generate a first expansion local image, processing the first expansion global image through a first encoder to generate a first global characterization vector, processing the second expansion global image and the first expansion local image through a second encoder to generate a second global characterization vector and a first local characterization vector, comparing at least the first global characterization vector and the second global characterization vector to generate a global loss function, comparing at least the first global characterization vector and the first local characterization vector to generate a mixed loss function, and adjusting a second encoder according to the global loss function and the mixed loss function, wherein the first expansion pipeline is different from the second expansion pipeline.

In some embodiments, adjusting the second encoder in accordance with the global loss function and the hybrid loss function includes adding the global loss function and the hybrid loss function to generate a cross-view loss function, and adjusting the second encoder in accordance with the cross-view loss function.

In some embodiments, generating the first global image includes selecting a first scale value and a second scale value between a first clipping threshold scale and a second clipping threshold scale, and clipping the original image according to the first scale value and the second scale value, wherein the first clipping threshold scale is smaller than the second clipping threshold scale.

In some embodiments, generating the first partial image includes selecting a third scale value and a fourth scale value between a third crop critical ratio and a fourth crop critical ratio, and cropping the original image according to the third scale value and the fourth scale value, wherein the third crop critical ratio is less than the fourth crop critical ratio, and the fourth crop critical ratio is equal to the first crop critical ratio.

In some embodiments, the machine learning method further includes processing the first global image through a third expansion pipeline to generate a third expanded global image, and processing the third expanded global image through a first encoder to generate a third global characterization vector, wherein generating the global loss function includes comparing at least the third global characterization vector and the second global characterization vector to generate a global loss function, generating the hybrid loss function includes comparing at least the third global characterization vector and the first local characterization vector to generate the hybrid loss function, and the first expansion pipeline, the second expansion pipeline, and the third expansion pipeline are different from one another.

In some embodiments, the machine learning method further includes cropping the original image to generate a second global image, processing the second global image through a first expansion pipeline and a second expansion pipeline to generate a first set of expanded global images, processing at least the first set of expanded global images through a first encoder to generate a first set of global characterization vectors, processing the second global image through a third expansion pipeline and a fourth expansion pipeline to generate a second set of expanded global images, processing at least the second set of expanded global images through a second encoder to generate a second set of global characterization vectors, and comparing the first set of global characterization vectors and the second set of global characterization vectors to generate global loss functions, wherein the first set of global characterization vectors and the second set of global characterization vectors respectively include a first global characterization vector and a second global characterization vector, and the first expansion pipeline, the second expansion pipeline, the third expansion pipeline, and the fourth expansion pipeline are different from each other.

In some embodiments, the machine learning method further includes cropping the original image to generate a second partial image, processing the second partial image through a first expansion pipe, a second expansion pipe, a third expansion pipe, and a fourth expansion pipe to generate a first expanded partial image set, processing at least the first expanded partial image set through a second encoder to generate a first partial characterization vector set, and comparing the first global characterization vector set and the first partial characterization vector set to generate a blending loss function, wherein the first partial characterization vector set includes the first partial characterization vector.

Embodiments of the present disclosure include a machine learning method. The machine learning method comprises the steps of cutting an original image to generate a first global image and a second global image, cutting the original image to generate a first local image and a second local image, processing the first global image and the second global image through an expansion pipeline to generate a first expanded global image and a second expanded global image, processing the first expanded global image and the second expanded global image through a first coder to generate a first global characterization vector and a second global characterization vector, processing the first expanded local image and the second expanded local image through a second coder to generate a first local characterization vector and a second local characterization vector, comparing at least the first global characterization vector, the second global characterization vector, the first local characterization vector and the second local characterization vector to generate a mixed loss function, and adjusting the second coder according to the mixed loss function.

In some embodiments, the machine learning method further includes cropping the original image to produce a third global image and a fourth global image, processing the third global image and the fourth global image through an expansion pipeline to produce a third expanded global image and a fourth expanded global image, processing the third expanded global image and the fourth expanded global image through a second encoder to produce a third global characterization vector and a fourth global characterization vector, comparing at least the first global characterization vector, the second global characterization vector, the third global characterization vector, the fourth global characterization vector to produce a global loss function, and adding the global loss function and the blend loss function to produce a cross-view loss function, wherein adjusting the second encoder includes adjusting the second encoder according to the cross-view loss function.

Detailed Description

Various embodiments of the present invention are disclosed in the accompanying drawings, and for purposes of clarity, numerous practical details are set forth in the following description. However, it should be understood that these practical details are not to be construed as limiting the present disclosure. That is, in some embodiments of the present disclosure, these practical details are unnecessary. In addition, for the sake of simplicity of the drawing, some of the conventional structures and elements are shown in the drawing in a simplified schematic manner.

Fig. 1 is a schematic diagram of a method 100 for processing an image according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. In some embodiments, method 100 may be performed by a memory, a processor, and/or various processing circuits (not shown). As shown in FIG. 1, the method 100 may include operations OP11 through OP15.

In operation OP11, the processor is configured to crop the original image OM1 to generate the global image GM1. In some embodiments, the processor randomly selects two scale values GR11 and GR12 (not shown) between the cut critical scales CTHR1 and CTHR (not shown). Wherein the cut-off critical ratio CTHR1 is less than the cut-off critical ratio CTHR.

Then, the processor is configured to randomly select a location LC11 in the original image OM1, and cut the original image OM1 according to the scale values GR11 and GR12 to generate a global image GM1. The length of the global image GM1 is the length of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value GR11, and the width of the global image GM1 is the width of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value GR12. In the embodiment shown in fig. 1, the length corresponds to the vertical direction and the width corresponds to the horizontal direction.

For example, the cut threshold ratios CTHR and CTHR2 may be 0.3 and 1.0, respectively. The processor selects two values, e.g., 0.4 and 0.9, between the cut-off threshold ratios CTHR and CTHR as the ratio values GR11 and GR12, respectively. Correspondingly, the length of the global image GM1 is 0.4 times the length of the original image OM1, and the width of the global image GM1 is 0.9 times the width of the original image OM 1.

In operation OP12, the processor is configured to crop the original image OM1 to generate the partial image LM1. In some embodiments, the processor randomly selects two scale values LR11 and LR12 (not shown) between the cut-off threshold scales CTHR and CTHR (not shown). Wherein the cut-off critical ratio CTHR is less than the cut-off critical ratio CTHR. In some embodiments, cut critical ratio CTHR4 is equal to cut critical ratio CTHR1.

Then, the processor is configured to randomly select a position LC12 in the original image OM1, and cut the original image OM1 according to the scale values LR11 and LR12 to generate the partial image LM1. The length of the partial image LM1 is the length of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR11, and the width of the partial image LM1 is the width of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR12.

For example, the cut threshold ratios CTHR and CTHR4 may be 0.1 and 0.3, respectively. The processor selects two values, e.g., 0.15 and 0.2, between the cut-off threshold ratios CTHR and CTHR as the ratio values LR11 and LR12, respectively. Correspondingly, the length of the partial image LM1 is 0.15 times the length of the original image OM1, and the width of the partial image LM1 is 0.2 times the width of the original image OM 1.

Similarly, in operation OP13, the processor is configured to crop the original image OM1 to generate the partial image LM2. In some embodiments, the processor randomly selects two ratio values LR13 and LR14 between the cut critical ratios CTHR and CTHR.

Then, the processor is configured to randomly select the position LC13 in the original image OM1, and cut the original image OM1 according to the scale values LR13 and LR14 to generate the partial image LM2. The length of the partial image LM2 is the length of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR13, and the width of the partial image LM2 is the width of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR14.

Similarly, in operation OP14, the processor is configured to crop the original image OM1 to generate the partial image LM3. In some embodiments, the processor randomly selects two scale values LR15 and LR16 between the cut critical scales CTHR and CTHR.

Then, the processor is configured to randomly select the position LC14 in the original image OM1, and cut the original image OM1 according to the scale values LR15 and LR16 to generate the partial image LM3. The length of the partial image LM3 is the length of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR15, and the width of the partial image LM3 is the width of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR16.

Similarly, in operation OP15, the processor is configured to crop the original image OM1 to generate the partial image LM4. In some embodiments, the processor randomly selects two scale values LR17 and LR18 between the cut critical scales CTHR and CTHR.

Then, the processor is configured to randomly select the position LC15 in the original image OM1, and cut the original image OM1 according to the scale values LR17 and LR18 to generate the partial image LM4. The length of the partial image LM4 is the length of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR17, and the width of the partial image LM3 is the width of the original image OM1 multiplied by the scale value LR18. In some embodiments, the partial images LM 1-LM 4 are different from each other.

In various embodiments, the cut critical ratio CTHR to CTHR may have various values. For example, the cut critical ratio CTHR may be 0.4, 0.3, or 0.5. The cut critical ratio CTHR may be 0.1 or 0.2. The cut critical ratio CTHR4 may be 0.4, 0.3, or 0.5. Among the settings that perform well are cut critical ratio CTHR and CTHR of 0.3 each, cut critical ratio CTHR2 of 1.0 and cut critical ratio CTHR of 0.1.

In some embodiments, the method 100 may be used to generate a plurality of cropped extended images of the global viewpoint and the local viewpoint, such as the global image GM1 and the local images LM 1-LM 4. Correspondingly, the method 100 may be referred to as a multi-view crop extension method.

Fig. 2 is a schematic diagram of a method 200 of processing an image according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. In some embodiments, method 200 may be performed by a memory, a processor, and/or various processing circuits (not shown). As shown in FIG. 2, the method 200 may include operations OP21 through OP26.

In operation OP21, the processor is configured to crop the original image OM2 to generate the partial image PM21. Referring to fig. 1 and 2, the original image OM2 is an embodiment of the original image OM1, the partial image PM21 is an embodiment of one of the global image GM1 and the partial images LM1 to LM4, and the operation OP21 is an embodiment of one of the operations OP11 to OP 15. Therefore, a part of the description will not be repeated.

In operation OP22, the processor processes the original image OM2 by the heuristic mask generator to generate a mask image MM2. The mask image MM2 includes a white portion WP21 corresponding to the foreground and a black portion BP21 corresponding to the background. In some embodiments, the white portion WP21 has a logical value of 1 and the black portion BP21 has a logical value of 0.

In operation OP23, the processor is configured to cut the mask image MM2 according to the relationship between the partial image PM21 and the original image OM2 to generate the partial mask image PMM21. The position and area of the partial image PM21 on the original image OM2 are equal to the position and area of the partial mask image PMM21 on the mask image MM 2. The partial mask image PMM21 includes a white portion WP22 corresponding to the foreground and a black portion BP22 corresponding to the background.

In operation OP24, the processor is configured to determine the foreground rate of the partial image PM21 according to the white portion WP22 and the black portion BP22, and compare the foreground rate of the partial image PM21 with a preset foreground rate. When the foreground rate of the partial image PM21 is greater than the preset foreground rate, the processor performs an operation OP25 after the operation OP 24. When the foreground rate of the partial image PM21 is less than or equal to the preset foreground rate, the processor performs an operation OP26 after the operation OP 24.

In some embodiments, the foreground rate is the area of the white portion WP22 divided by the area of the partial mask image PMM 21. Wherein the area of the partial mask image PMM21 is the area of the white portion WP22 plus the area of the black portion BP 22. In some embodiments, the preset foreground rate is 0.3.

In operation OP25, the processor determines that the partial image PM21 is a valid cropped image, and performs subsequent operations on the partial image PM21, such as operations OP 54-OP 58 shown in fig. 5.

In operation OP26, the processor discards the partial image PM21, e.g., deletes the partial image PM21 from memory. After operation OP26, the processor re-performs operation OP21 to re-crop the new partial image to perform operations OP 22-OP 24 again.

For example, after the processor discards the partial image PM21, the processor cuts the original image OM2 again to generate the partial image PM22, and proceeds to the OP23 again to generate the partial mask image PMM22 corresponding to the partial image PM 22. Next, the processor performs an operation OP24 on the partial mask image PMM22.

Fig. 3A is a schematic diagram of a method 300 of generating an extended image according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. As shown in FIG. 3A, the method 300 may include operating OP 31-OP 36.

In operation OP31, the processor is configured to generate the cut images CM31 and CM32. Referring to fig. 1 to 3A, operation OP31 may be performed by a portion or all of methods 100 and 200. The cut images CM31 and CM32 may be embodiments of partial images PM21, PM22, global image GM1, and partial images LM 1-LM 4.

At operation OP32, the processor is configured to select one expansion pipe from a plurality of expansion pipes that are different from each other. In the embodiment shown in FIG. 3A, the processor stores four expansion pipelines, namely an Auto-Augment pipeline, a Fast Auto-Augment pipeline, a SimCLR expansion pipeline, and a random expansion (Random Augment) pipeline. However, the present disclosure is not limited thereto. In various embodiments, the selection may also be made among various numbers of expansion pipes.

Next, in operation OP33, in response to the processor selecting SimCLR the expansion pipe, the processor performs expansion processing on the cut images CM31 and CM32 with SimCLR expansion pipe to generate expanded images AM31 and AM32, respectively.

Similarly, at operation OP34, in response to the processor selecting the random expansion pipe, the processor performs expansion processing on the cut images CM31 and CM32 with the random expansion pipe to generate expanded images AM33 and AM34, respectively.

Similarly, in operation OP35, in response to the processor selecting the auto-expansion pipe, the processor performs expansion processing on the cut images CM31 and CM32 with the auto-expansion pipe to generate expanded images AM35 and AM36, respectively.

Similarly, at operation OP36, in response to the processor selecting the quick auto-expansion pipe, the processor expands the cut images CM31 and CM32 with the quick auto-expansion pipe to generate expanded images AM37 and AM38, respectively.

In some implementations, the expanded images are generated manually, so that the differences between the expanded images are small.

In contrast to the above, in the embodiments of the present disclosure, the processor generates the expanded images AM 31-AM 38 through four different expansion pipelines. Thus, the difference between the expanded images AM 31-AM 38 is larger.

Fig. 3B is a schematic diagram illustrating further details of the operation OP35 shown in fig. 3A according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. In some embodiments, the operation OP35 is used to perform expansion processing on the cut image CM33 to generate an expanded image AM39. Referring to fig. 3A and 3B, the cut image CM33 is an embodiment of the cut image CM31 or CM32, and the expanded image AM39 is an embodiment of the expanded image AM35 or AM 36.

As shown in FIG. 3B, operations OP35 may include operations OP 351-OP 352. At operation OP35, in response to the processor selecting the auto-expansion pipe, the processor randomly selects one sub-policy from a plurality of sub-policies contained in the auto-expansion pipe. In the embodiment shown in FIG. 3B, the processor selects a sub-strategy that includes operations OP 351-OP 352.

In operation OP351, the processor equalizes the cut image CM33 with the intensity 7 to generate the expanded image AM310.

In operation OP352, the processor exposes the expanded image AM310 with intensity 4 to generate an expanded image AM39.

In other embodiments, the processor may also select other sub-policies from among the plurality of sub-policies contained in the auto-expanding pipeline. For example, in response to selecting another sub-strategy, the processor may tone separate the cropped image CM33 at intensity 8 and rotate it at intensity 9 to produce the expanded image AM39.

Similarly, the fast auto-expansion pipe and the random expansion pipe may also contain multiple sub-policies. Correspondingly, operations similar to OP35 may also be performed in operations OP34 and OP36.

Fig. 4A is a schematic diagram of a machine learning method 400A according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. Referring to fig. 4A and 1, the machine learning method 400A includes operations OP11 and OP12 for cropping the original image OM1 to generate the global image GM1 and the local image LM 1. In addition, the machine learning method 400A further includes operations OP 41-OP 45.

In operation OP41, the processor processes the global image GM1 through the auto-expansion pipeline to generate an expanded global image AGM41, processes the global image GM1 through the random expansion pipeline to generate an expanded global image AGM42, processes the global image GM1 through the fast auto-expansion pipeline to generate an expanded global image AGM43, and processes the global image GM1 through the SimCLR expansion pipeline to generate an expanded global image AGM44.

In addition, in operation OP41, the processor processes the local image LM1 through the auto-expansion pipeline to generate an expanded local image ALM41, processes the local image LM1 through the random expansion pipeline to generate an expanded local image ALM42, processes the local image LM1 through the fast auto-expansion pipeline to generate an expanded local image ALM43, and processes the local image LM1 through the SimCLR expansion pipeline to generate an expanded local image ALM44.

In some embodiments, parameters of the sub-policies included in the auto-expansion pipeline are generated by the processor training from the data set including the original image OM1 prior to performing the method 400A. On the other hand, parameters of the sub-policies contained in the random expansion pipeline are randomly generated when the operation OP41 is performed. In other words, the parameters of the auto-expansion pipeline are related to the original image OM1, and the parameters of the random expansion pipeline are not related to the original image OM1 and are generated after the parameters of the auto-expansion pipeline are generated.

In some embodiments, the parameters of the sub-policies included in the fast auto-expansion pipeline and the parameters of the sub-policies included in the SimCLR expansion pipeline are also generated by the processor training based on the data set including the original image OM1 before executing the method 400A.

In operation OP42, the encoder EC42 processes the expanded global images AGM43, AGM44 and the expanded local images ALM 41-ALM 44 to generate a plurality of corresponding feature maps FM42.

In operation OP43, the encoder EC41 processes the expanded global images AGM41 and AGM42 to generate a plurality of corresponding feature maps FM41.

In some embodiments, encoders EC41 and EC42 are related to each other by the following equation (1):

ξ←τξ+(1-τ)θ(1)

where ζ is a parameter of the encoder EC41, θ is a parameter of the encoder EC42, and τ is a parameter of a correlation between the encoders EC41 and EC 42.

In operation OP44, the processor sequentially processes the feature map FM42 through the neural networks MLP41 and MLP42 to generate the corresponding global characterization vectors GV43, GV44 and local characterization vectors LV41 to LV44. The global characterization vectors GV43, GV44 and the local characterization vectors LV 41-LV 44 correspond to the expanded global images AGM43, AGM44 and the expanded local images ALM 41-ALM 44, respectively.

In operation OP45, the processor processes the feature map FM41 through the neural network MLP43 to generate the corresponding global token vectors GV41 and GV42. Wherein the global characterization vectors GV41 and GV42 correspond to the expanded global images AGM41 and AGM42, respectively.

The processor may then compare global token vectors GV41, GV42 with global token vectors GV43, GV44 to generate global loss function GL4, and compare global token vectors GV41, GV42 with local token vectors LV 41-LV 44 to generate mixed loss function ML4.

For example, the larger the similarity between the global token vectors GV41, GV42 and the global token vectors GV43, GV44, the smaller the value of the global loss function GL 4. The smaller the value of the blending loss function ML4, the greater the similarity between the global characterization vectors GV41, GV42 and the local characterization vectors LV 41-LV 44.

In some embodiments, the processor is also configured to add the global loss function GL4 and the blend loss function ML4 to generate a cross-view loss function CVL4 (not shown). The processor is then further configured to adjust the weighting parameters of the encoder EC42 according to the cross-view loss function CVL 4.

For example, the processor may perform operations OP 42-OP 45 again through the adjusted encoder EC42 after adjusting the weight parameters of the encoder EC42 to generate a new cross-view loss function CVL4. In some embodiments, the processor may gradually adjust the weight parameters of encoder EC42 until cross-view loss function CVL4 has a minimum.

In some embodiments, at intervals, the processor copies the adjusted weight parameters of encoder EC42 to encoder EC41 such that the weight parameters of encoder EC41 may be adjusted accordingly. In other words, the weight parameters of the encoder EC41 can also be adjusted by the encoder EC42 according to the cross-view loss function CVL 4. In some embodiments, the above-described operation of adjusting the weight parameters is referred to as training encoders EC41 and EC 42.

In some embodiments, the neural networks MLP 41-MLP 43 may be implemented by multi-layer perceptrons (Multilayer perceptron, MLP). For example, the neural network MLPs 41 and 43 may be implemented by a mapper (projector), and the neural network MLP42 may be implemented by a predictor.

In some embodiments, after training the encoder EC41 or EC42, the processor may apply the actual to downstream tasks, such as tasks to determine whether the image belongs to a certain category. In performing the downstream tasks, the encoder EC41 or EC42 outputs the feature maps into the neural network corresponding to the downstream tasks.

In the embodiment shown in fig. 4A, the processor processes the single global image GM1 and the single local image LM1 with multiple expansion pipelines. Correspondingly, in some embodiments, the machine learning method 400A is referred to as a multi-augmented single-view machine learning method.

In some implementations, the extended images are generated by a single extended pipeline, so that the differences between the extended images are small.

In contrast to the above, in the embodiments of the present disclosure, the processor generates the expanded global images AGM 41-AGM 44 and the expanded local images ALM 41-ALM 44 through four different expansion pipelines. Thus, the difference between the expanded global images AGM41 to AGM44 and the expanded local images ALM41 to ALM44 is large.

Fig. 4B is a schematic diagram of a machine learning method 400B according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. Referring to fig. 4A and 4B, a machine learning method 400B is a variation of the machine learning method 400A. Therefore, for the sake of brevity, some details will not be repeated.

In contrast to the machine learning method 400A, in the machine learning method 400B, the processor performs a plurality of operations OP11 to generate a plurality of global images GM 1-GM 4 and performs operations OP 12-OP 14 to generate a plurality of local images LM 1-LM 4.

In contrast to the machine learning method 400A, the machine learning method 400B includes an operation OB41 instead of an operation OP41. In operation OB41, the processor processes the global images GM 1-GM 4 and the local images LM 1-LM 4 through the auto-expansion pipeline to generate expanded global images AGM 41-AGM 44 and expanded local images ALM 41-ALM 44, respectively.

Then, the processor performs operations OP 42-OP 45 on the expanded global images AGM 41-AGM 44 and the expanded local images ALM 41-ALM 44 to train the encoders EC41 and EC42. Details of the operations OP42 to OP45 are described above in the embodiment of fig. 4A, and thus are not repeated.

In the embodiment shown in fig. 4B, the processor processes the global images GM1 to GM4 and the local images LM1 to LM4 with a single expansion pipeline. Correspondingly, in some embodiments, the machine learning method 400B is referred to as a single extended multi-view machine learning method.

In some implementations, when the encoder is trained, only the images from a single viewpoint are trained, making the training result worse.

In contrast to the above, in the embodiment of the present disclosure, the processor trains through the global images GM1 to GM4 and the local images LM1 to LM 4. Thus, the training result is better.

Fig. 5 is a schematic diagram of a machine learning method 500 according to some embodiments of the present disclosure. As shown in FIG. 5, the machine learning method 500 includes operations OP 51-OP 58.

In operation OP51, the processor cuts the original image OM1 according to the cut-off threshold ratios CTHR and CTHR to generate a plurality of global images.

In operation OP52, the processor cuts the original image OM1 according to the cut critical proportions CTHR and CTHR to generate a plurality of partial images.

Referring to fig. 1 and 5, operation OP51 is similar to operation OP11, and operation OP52 is similar to operations OP 12-OP 15. Therefore, for brevity, some descriptions will not be repeated.

At operation OP53, the processor checks whether the global image and the local image generated at operations OP51 and OP52 are valid cropped images. When the global image generated by the operation OP51 is a valid cropped image, the processor is configured to output valid global images (e.g., global images GM1 and GM 2) for subsequent operations. When the partial image generated by the operation OP52 is a valid cropped image, the processor is configured to output valid partial images (e.g., partial images LM1 to LM 6) for subsequent operations.

In the embodiment shown in fig. 5, at operation OP54, the processor processes the global image GM1 through the auto-expansion pipeline and the random-expansion pipeline to generate two expanded global images in the expanded global image group AGG1, and processes the global image GM2 through the auto-expansion pipeline and the random-expansion pipeline to generate two expanded global images in the expanded global image group AGG 2.

Similarly, at operation OP54, the processor processes the global image GM1 through the fast auto-expansion pipeline and the SimCLR expansion pipeline to generate two expanded global images in the expanded global image group AGG3, and processes the global image GM2 through the fast auto-expansion pipeline and the SimCLR expansion pipeline to generate two expanded global images in the expanded global image group AGG4, respectively.

Similarly, at operation OP54, the processor processes the local image LM1 through the auto-expansion pipeline, the random expansion pipeline, the fast auto-expansion pipeline, and the SimCLR expansion pipeline, respectively, to generate four expanded global images in the expanded local image group ALG 1.

Similarly, at operation OP54, the processor processes the local image LM2 through the auto-expansion pipeline, the random expansion pipeline, the fast auto-expansion pipeline, and the SimCLR expansion pipeline, respectively, to generate four expanded global images in the expanded local image group ALG 2.

Similarly, at operation OP54, the processor processes the local image LM3 through the auto-expansion pipeline, the random expansion pipeline, the fast auto-expansion pipeline, and the SimCLR expansion pipeline, respectively, to generate four expanded global images in the expanded local image group ALG 3.

Similarly, at operation OP54, the processor processes the local image LM4 through the auto-expansion pipeline, the random expansion pipeline, the fast auto-expansion pipeline, and the SimCLR expansion pipeline, respectively, to generate four expanded global images in the expanded local image group ALG 4.

Similarly, at operation OP54, the processor processes the local image LM5 through the auto-expansion pipeline, the random expansion pipeline, the fast auto-expansion pipeline, and the SimCLR expansion pipeline, respectively, to generate four expanded global images in the expanded local image group ALG 5.

Similarly, at operation OP54, the processor processes the local image LM6 through the auto-expansion pipeline, the random expansion pipeline, the fast auto-expansion pipeline, and the SimCLR expansion pipeline, respectively, to generate four expanded global images in the expanded local image group ALG 6.

Referring to fig. 4A and 5, the extended global images AGM41 and AGM42 may be included in the extended global image group AGG1, the extended global images AGM43 and AGM44 may be included in the extended global image group AGG2, and the extended local images ALM41 to ALM44 may be included in the extended local image group ALG1.

Next, in operation OP55, the encoder EC42 processes the extended global image groups AGG3, AGG4 and the extended local image groups ALG 1-ALG 6 to generate a plurality of corresponding feature maps FM52.

In operation OP56, the encoder EC41 processes the extended global image groups AGG1 and AGG2 to generate a plurality of corresponding feature maps FM51.

Referring to fig. 4A and 5, the feature map FM41 may be included in the feature map FM51, and the feature map FM42 may be included in the feature map FM52.

In operation OP57, the processor sequentially processes the feature map FM52 through the neural networks MLP41 and MLP42 to generate the corresponding global token vector set GVG2 and local token vector set LVG1. The global token vector group GVG2 corresponds to the extended global image groups AGG3 and AGG4, and the local token vector group LVG1 corresponds to the extended local image groups ALG1 to ALG6.

In operation OP58, the processor processes the feature map FM51 through the neural network MLP43 to generate a corresponding global token vector group GVG1. The global token vector group GVG1 corresponds to the extended global image groups AGG1 and AGG2.

Referring to fig. 4A and 5, global token vectors GV41 and GV42 may be included in global token vector group GVG1, global token vectors GV43 and GV44 may be included in global token vector group GVG2, and local token vectors LV41 to LV44 may be included in local token vector group LVG1.

The processor may then compare global token vector group GVG1 with global token vector group GVG2 to generate global loss function GL5, and compare global token vector group GVG1 with local token vector group LVG1 to generate mixed loss function ML5.

For example, the larger the similarity between the global token vector group GVG1 and the global token vector group GVG2, the smaller the value of the global loss function GL 5. The smaller the value of the blending loss function ML5, the greater the similarity between the global token vector group GVG1 and the local token vector group LVG 1.

In some embodiments, the processor is also configured to add the global loss function GL5 and the blend loss function ML5 to generate a cross-view loss function CVL5 (not shown). The processor is then further configured to adjust the weighting parameters of the encoder EC42 according to the cross-view loss function CVL 5.

For example, the processor may perform operations OP 55-OP 58 again through the adjusted encoder EC42 after adjusting the weight parameters of the encoder EC42 to generate a new cross-view loss function CVL5. In some embodiments, the processor may gradually adjust the weight parameters of encoder EC42 until cross-view loss function CVL5 has a minimum.
